## Research projects

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
Manuscript in preparation
:::

[Cross-Country Transfer Learning for ICU Admission Prediction](project-icu-transfer.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
PLACEHOLDER: author list · S-LAB, Jeonbuk National University · Feb 2026 – present
:::

Tests whether a clinical prediction model trained on one country's electronic
health records still works in another, and how much target-country data is
needed to close the gap. Built on TabPFN, with a label-noise analysis to check
that the reported gains are real.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-icu-transfer.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
University of Nevada, Las Vegas · 2025
:::

[Deep Neural Networks for Mortality Prediction from EHR Vital-Sign Time Series](project-ehr-mortality.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
Team project
:::

Predicts patient mortality from irregularly sampled vital signs at a Brazilian
cancer center, crossing two interpolation schemes with two network
architectures. The convolutional models won on every metric.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-ehr-mortality.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

## Conference presentations

::: {.research-card .accent-amber}

::: {.research-label}
IC-KDA + ASAD 2025 · Best Poster Award
:::

[Effectiveness of Digital Cognitive Training Interventions for Dementia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis](project-dementia-meta.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
J. Sung, *N.-Y. Kim* · May 2025, Seoul
:::

A PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis of eleven randomized trials asking whether
remotely delivered cognitive training improves cognitive and depressive outcomes
in dementia. It improved both, on a small evidence base.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-dementia-meta.qmd){.research-btn}
[PROSPERO](https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=631806){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card .accent-rust}

::: {.research-label}
Korean Statistical Society Summer Conference 2025
:::

[Deep Learning-based Neural Granger Causality for Solar Radiation Time Series](project-granger.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
M. Lee, S. Lee, Y. Cho, *N.-Y. Kim*, G. Kim, Y. Lee · June 2025, Gyeongju
:::

Asks which meteorological variables carry predictive information about solar
radiation, and whether neural Granger causality recovers relationships a linear
vector autoregression misses. It does, for the variables that behave least like
continuous measurements.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-granger.qmd){.research-btn}
:::
